Fit the additive measurement-error model (signal + measurement variance)

Source: R/fit_additive_weight.R
fit_additive_weight.Rd

Fits a Bayesian Gaussian model in which each observation's variance is the sum of true between-subject variance and measurement variance, $$\sigma_i^2 = \tau^2 + \kappa^2\, se_i^{2\beta_1},$$ with a censored likelihood for samples outside the quantifiable range. It is the default estimator of fit_precision_weights() from curveRweights 0.3.0.

Usage

fit_additive_weight(
  df,
  cell_col = "cell",
  concentration_col = "predicted_concentration",
  se_col = "se_concentration",
  plate_col = "plate",
  patient_col = NULL,
  sample_col = NULL,
  censor_col = NULL,
  lower_col = "censor_lower",
  upper_col = "censor_upper",
  se_bound_col = NULL,
  dilution_col = NULL,
  response_is_log10 = FALSE,
  fix_beta1 = TRUE,
  prior_location = brms::set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "b"),
  prior_ltau = brms::set_prior("normal(-1.2, 1)", class = "b", nlpar = "ltau"),
  prior_lkappa = brms::set_prior("normal(0, 0.5)", class = "b", nlpar = "lkappa"),
  prior_beta1 = brms::set_prior("normal(1, 0.25)", class = "b", nlpar = "beta1"),
  prior_group_sd = brms::set_prior("normal(0, 0.5)", class = "sd"),
  iter = 2000,
  warmup = 1000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.95,
  seed = 42,
  backend = NULL,
  n_draws_weights = 1000
)

Arguments

df

Data frame with observation-level data.

cell_col

Name of the saturated cell factor column.

concentration_col

Predicted concentration column.

se_col

Measurement SE column (log10 scale; the curveR se_concentration).

plate_col

Plate (or curve) grouping column; NULL for none.

patient_col

Subject grouping column; NULL for none. Strongly recommended when subjects are measured more than once.

sample_col

Optional column identifying a physical sample measured several times (dilutions/replicates).

censor_col

Name of the censoring-type column ("none", "left", "right", "interval"). NULL (default) treats every row as quantified.

lower_col, upper_col

Natural-scale censoring bounds.

se_bound_col

Optional measurement SE at the censoring limit; see prepare_censoring().

dilution_col

Optional dilution-factor column. If supplied, the response is converted to the final-concentration scale (yi + log10(dilution)), which is the scale curveRcore's censoring bounds are on. Supply it whenever you use curveRcore censoring bounds and dilutions differ.

response_is_log10

Is concentration_col already log10?

fix_beta1

Fix \(\beta_1 = 1\) (default) or estimate it.

prior_location, prior_ltau, prior_lkappa, prior_beta1, prior_group_sd

brms::prior objects.

iter, warmup, chains, cores, adapt_delta, seed

MCMC controls.

backend

Passed to brms::brm(); NULL uses the brms default.

n_draws_weights

Number of posterior draws used for the reliability interval (thinned from the fit).

Value

A list with fit, tau, tau2, kappa, beta1, their credible intervals (tau_CI, kappa_CI, beta1_CI), overall reliability and reliability_CI (\(\tau^2/(\tau^2 + \bar v)\) over quantified rows), data (the full input with the weight columns of compute_additive_weights()), diagnostics, formula and priors_used.

In plain terms

An assay value varies between subjects for two different reasons. Subjects truly differ (biology; this is the signal, variance \(\tau^2\)), and the calibration curve measures each sample with some error (variance \(v_i\), known to us through se_i). The two add. The older multiplicative model of curveRweights 0.2.x instead made the whole spread proportional to se, which implies that a precisely measured sample has little biological variation, so it could be given a weight many times larger than its neighbours. In the additive model the weight is at most \(1/\tau^2\); no sample can count for more than a perfectly measured one.

\(\kappa\) is a calibration factor: \(\kappa = 1\) means the reported se is exactly the measurement SD (the delta-method value). \(\beta_1\) is fixed at 1 by default; \(\kappa\) and \(\tau\) are separated only through the spread of se across samples, so freeing \(\beta_1\) as well makes the model much harder to identify. Use fix_beta1 = FALSE only with plenty of data over a wide range of se.

Model

Location: yi ~ 0 + cell + (1|patient) + (1|plate) [+ (1|sample)], where cell is the saturated design factor (e.g. arm by time point). The patient term absorbs correlation between repeated samples of the same subject (otherwise counted as noise); the optional sample term does the same for several dilutions or replicates of one physical sample.

Scale: \(\sigma_i = \sqrt{\tau^2 + \kappa^2 se_i^{2\beta_1}}\) via a non-linear sigma formula. Rows with censor_type left, right or interval contribute a cumulative-probability term at their censoring limit (see prepare_censoring()); quantified rows contribute a normal density.

Default priors: location normal(0, 2); \(\log\tau \sim N(\log 0.3, 1)\); \(\log\kappa \sim N(0, 0.5)\) (centred on the delta-method value); \(\beta_1 \sim N(1, 0.25)\) when free; group SDs normal(0, 0.5).
